title: Reading to Children in Japanese にほんご　おはなし会
description: Preschool age children and their parents/caregivers are invited to the West Valley Branch Library for Reading to Children in Japanese.
parentSummary: Preschool age children and their parents/caregivers are invited to the West Valley Branch Library for Reading to Children in Japanese.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Preschool age children and their parents/caregivers are invited to the West Valley Branch Library for Reading to Children in Japanese. Every Thursday at 11:00 AM, children will enjoy early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities all in the Japanese language. 
This program is brought to the library by Poponta Children's Cultural Society. Established in 2008 and based in San Mateo, Poponta is comprised of a group of volunteers dedicated to serving the Japanese-speaking community. Poponta volunteers tell stories to children to open their minds to the magic of books. To learn more about Poponta, please visit:nbsp;https://ja-jp.facebook.com/popontanokai/
Free, with limited capacity. Seating is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of the program. San José Public Library Early Education programs are in alignment with the City’s Education and Digital Literacy Initiative. 
 
ADA Accommodation Requests
 未就園児のお子さま、日本語に興味のあるお子さまとその保護者の皆さまは、ウェストバレーブランチ図書館日本語お話会にご参加いただけます。毎週木曜日の午前11時に、絵本の読みきかせ、手遊び歌、昔話、ペープサートなどが楽しめます。このプログラムは、ぽぽんた児童文化の会メンバーの一人と有志によって図書館で開催しています。 ぽぽんた児童文化の会は2008年に設立され、サンマテオを拠点とし、ベイエリアにお住まいの日本語を話すコミュニティに日本文化、日本語のお話を提供するボランティアグループです。パンデミック中の規則に準拠し、ストーリータイム(お話会)においてもいくつかルールが変更になりましたのでご確認ください。これは屋内プログラムになることに注意してください。全員（2歳以上）は屋内でマスク着用をお勧めします。座席は先着順でご利用いただけます。プログラム開始30分前にインフォメーションデスクにて、数量限定のチケットを配布いたします。サンノゼ公立図書館の早期教育プログラムは、市の教育およびデジタルリテラシーイニシアチブと連携しています。図書館主催のイベントでは、アメリカ障害者法に基づく介助が必要な場合、イベントの少なくとも7営業日前に408-244-4747にお電話ください。

description: \nIn this workshop participants will create their own artwork using colorful fusion beads.

sourceDescriptionRaw:
Design and create small artworks using fuse beads (also known as Perler beads)!
In this workshop participants will create their own artwork using colorful fusion beads. This program introduces simple designs, pattern-building, and color planning. Participantsnbsp;can follow ready-made templates or create their own designs. After building their designs on the pegboards, we will safely fuse the beads with heat so everyone can take home their finished design for themselves or others.
Registration required: supplies are limited!
Recommended for ages 7 and up caregivers are welcomed to join; youngernbsp;children may need assistance from an adult.
ADA Accommodation Request
Tarde de manualidades: ¡Magia con cuentas de fusión!
¡Diseña y crea pequeñas obras de arte con cuentas de fusión (también conocidas como Perler Beads)!
En este taller, los participantes crearán sus propias obras de arte con cuentas de fusión de colores. Este programa introduce diseños sencillos, creación de patrones y planificación de colores. Los participantes pueden seguir plantillas prefabricadas o crear sus propios diseños. Después de construir sus diseños en los tableros perforados, fusionaremos las cuentas de forma segura con calor para que todos puedan llevarse a casa su diseño terminado, ya sea para sí mismos o para otros.
Se requiere inscripción: ¡suministros limitados!
Recomendado para niños a partir de 7 años. Los cuidadores pueden participar; los niños más pequeños podrían necesitar la ayuda de un adulto.

title: Intermediate Mass Black Holes; Meteor Showers or Space Debris?
description: In this talk, we explore how changes in visible gas emission lines over nearly two decades cannbsp;reveal these hidden engines, highlighting recent Magellan Spectrograph observations of dwarf galaxy J1143 that point to an accretingnbsp;intermediate-mass black hole at its core.
parentSummary: In this talk, we explore how changes in visible gas emission lines over nearly two decades cannbsp;reveal these hidden engines, highlighting recent Magellan Spectrograph observations of dwarf galaxy J1143 that point to an accretingnbsp;intermediate-mass black hole at its core.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Lecture 1:nbsp;nbsp;Understanding how supermassive black holes grow offers key clues to how galaxies evolve, but their "missing link"—intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs)—remains elusive. Because small, blue compact dwarf galaxies cannot host supermassive monsters, theynbsp;are prime hunting grounds for IMBHs. In this talk, we explore how changes in visible gas emission lines over nearly two decades cannbsp;reveal these hidden engines, highlighting recent Magellan Spectrograph observations of dwarf galaxy J1143 that point to an accretingnbsp;intermediate-mass black hole at its core. Delivered by Kiera Aston.\nLecture 2:nbsp;nbsp;Gorgeous meteor showers streaking across the zenith, or space trash entering our atmosphere? The 21st century’s growing “spacenbsp;environment” problem is beginning to take center stage. Space debris, artificial spacecraft and objects that have ceased functioning,nbsp;are accumulating in Low Earth Orbit at an unprecedented rate. We are developing a global space debris monitoring network usingnbsp;ground-based observations. At the core of the system is a three-channel multispectral camera designed to detect the aluminumnbsp;emission line in the near-UV spectrum, providing a distinctive signature for identifying space debris as it reenters Earth’s atmosphere.nbsp;Delivered by Alice Zou.\nFor accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+days prior to the event. If you need assistance with thenbsp;form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

title: The GreenRoots Collective: Environmental Technology Workshops
registrationEvidence: Microplastics Lab: Investigating Tiny Plastics in Our Environment - December 18 Ages: 7-12 Registration Recommended!
description: Each workshop introduces a scientific idea, gives students the opportunity to investigate it through a hands-on activity, and challenges them to apply what they learn to a practical solution.
parentSummary: Each workshop introduces a scientific idea, gives students the opportunity to investigate it through a hands-on activity, and challenges them to apply what they learn to a practical solution.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Discover how science and engineering can be used to understand and solve real environmental challenges. In this hands-on GreenRoots Collective workshop series, students will explore sustainability through interactive experiments, engineering challenges, collaborative problem-solving, and community-focused projects.
Sustainability is becoming an increasingly important part of the world students are growing up in. Understanding how the environment works, and how everyday decisions, technology, and engineering can help protect it, gives young learners the tools to think critically about real-world problems and envision better solutions for the future.
Rather than simply learning environmental concepts, students will put them into practice. Each workshop introduces a scientific idea, gives students the opportunity to investigate it through a hands-on activity, and challenges them to apply what they learn to a practical solution. Students will also contribute to community projects that connect their learning to meaningful action beyond the classroom. Through the program, participants will strengthen scientific reasoning, engineering design, creativity, teamwork, and problem-solving skills while developing a deeper understanding of sustainability and how STEM can be used to create positive change.
Series Topics:
1. Floodproof! The Science Engineering of El Niño - November 82. Cooler Cities: Engineering Solutions to Urban Heat - November 203. Clean Air Lab: The Science of Pollution Filtration - December 134. Microplastics Lab: Investigating Tiny Plastics in Our Environment - December 18
Ages: 7-12
Registration Recommended!

title: Beyond The Spotlight: One Life. Multiple Passions. Endless Possibilities.
description: \nThrough personal stories, practical insights, and thoughtful conversation, this event invites participants to rethink traditional career paths, make space for creativity, and redefine what success can look like.
parentSummary: \nThrough personal stories, practical insights, and thoughtful conversation, this event invites participants to rethink traditional career paths, make space for creativity, and redefine what success can look like.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
In this inspiring talk with professionals, we explore how passion for the performing arts can coexist with a primary career. Can you be a professional by day and a performer by choice? What does it look like when theater becomes more than a hobby without becoming your full-time profession?
Through personal stories, practical insights, and thoughtful conversation, this event invites participants to rethink traditional career paths, make space for creativity, and redefine what success can look like. We will discuss how aspiring performers can balance education, professional goals, personal responsibilities, and their love for the stage.
Join us for a thought-provoking discussion on pursuing Performing Arts and Theater as a Parallel Career Path: an exploration of passion, purpose, possibility, and the courage to embrace more than one professional identity.Carla PantojaCarla, born and raised in the South Bay, is an actor, fight director, teaching artist, intimacy director, and mom of two. She has been a Resident Artist of San Francisco Shakespeare Festival since 2014 and recently served as Director of Vision for the 2021 Free Shakespeare in the Park production of Pericles, Prince of Tyre, directing episodes 2 and 4. In 2020, she was in the acting company at Oregon Shakespeare Festival, returning in 2022 as the festival’s first female fight director. Carla is an associate instructor for Dueling Arts International and serves on their governing body as President. She is also a proud member of Making Good Trouble, an anti-racist training cohort based in the Bay Area. Carla has directed SF Shakes Shakespeare on Tour production of Romeo and Juliet and Comedy of Errors and Assistant Directed the 2017 Free Shakespeare in the Park production of Hamlet. She played Paulina in Free Shakespeare in the Park’s The Winter’s Tale, Tybalt in Romeo and Juliet, and Kate in The Taming of the Shrew. She’s performed with Cal Shakes, Shotgun Players, Crowded Fire, Playground, Lorraine Hansberry Theatre, and the SF Mime Troupe in the Bay Area to name a few.Vinay PandeVinay Pande is a Silicon Valley technology leader and a passionate theatre artist who brings together the worlds of innovation and performing arts. Originally from Mumbai, India, Vinay holds a degree in Instrumentation Engineering and began his career in telecommunications, where he was part of the core team that developed India’s first satellite-based mission-critical voice, data, and video network for the Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO). He later worked as a researcher at the prestigious Bell Labs and holds 15 technology patents, and co-authored technical publications and books. Today, he serves as a Principal Architect at a leading technology company in Silicon Valley.
Beyond his technology career, Vinay has nurtured a deep passion for the performing arts for over a decade, actively pursuing theatre, acting, and singing across Marathi and Hindi productions. From bringing diverse characters to life on stage to engaging audiences as a Radio Jockey and event host, he thrives on the energy of live performance and the magic of storytelling. For Vinay, technology may be his profession, but the stage is where his creative spirit truly comes alive.Sowmya Renukuntla
Sowmya is a Bay Area native and recent graduate from Santa Clara University, where she studied Business and worked directly with Admission Counselors for four years. Since graduating, she has been working full-time at Levi Strauss Co. on the Corporate Insights team and is a part-time college counselor.Sponsored by the Cupertino Library Foundation.nbsp;For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

sourceDescriptionRaw: Today's Hours: See Calendar Open select evenings, Nov 21 - Dec 31 Enjoy the magic of North Pole Nights and unlimited visits in 2027! Open select evenings, Nov 21 - Dec 31 Enjoy the magic of North Pole Nights and unlimited visits in 2027! Today's Hours: See Calendar Select Dates, November 21 - December 31 The North Pole magic will be returning to Gilroy Gardens this holiday season! Get into the holiday spirit as you immerse yourself in the enchanting world of North Pole Nights on select evenings from November 21 through December 31. This extraordinary experience includes jolly characters, fun live shows, ice skating under the stars, festive food and drinks, magical light displays and much, much more! The following rides will be closed during this Signature Event: Rainbow Garden Round Boat Ride, Paddle Boats, and Sky Trail Monorail Once you’ve made the trek across Candy Cane Lane bridge, you’ll find yourself in the festive world of North Pole Village with a chance to meet some of Santa’s merry, mischievous elves! You’ll find plenty of beautiful light displays throughout the park. Be prepared to “ooh” and “ahh” as you walk through this festive 100-foot-long animated musical Tunnel of Lights! Have you been good this year? Stop by one of the North Pole Post Office locations to write down your perfect wish for Christmas, then put it in the mailbox to send to Santa! Eat, drink, and be merry during North Pole Nights! Discover delicious holiday treats, cozy warm beverages, and festive cocktails and mocktails throughout the park. Satisfy your holiday cravings with delicious seasonal treats and festive food throughout the park! Warm up with a delicious hot beverage from Skitter's Cozy Cabin, the perfect way to stay warm on a chilly winter night! Find festive mocktails, cocktails, and warm beverages at our 3 bars: Skitter's Cozy Cabin, Live Tonight Bar, and Merry & Mischief Bar. The North Pole is the perfect place to practice your ice skating skills! Stop by the ice rink as you cross Candy Cane Lane into the North Pole Village. Already have a pair of skates? Simply fill out a waiver to skate FREE! See our staff at the ice rink for more info. Add a little extra magic to your holiday season with a North Pole Nights Bubble Wand! Choose from two festive favorites, a cheerful Reindeer or a classic Nutcracker, and fill the air with holiday bubbles! December 19 & 20 | 5, 6 & 7 PM Back by popular demand! Gather your loved ones for a traditional holiday feast featuring roasted turkey, honey baked ham, garlic mashed potatoes, stuffing, and all the trimmings. Kids Under 12 Eat FREE! December 12 & 13 | 1-3 PM Enjoy a special storytime, a fun Christmas craft activity, and a delicious holiday lunch featuring ham, French toast, Green Eggs Scramble, and festive treats. Kids Under 12 Eat FREE! Rudy the Polar Bear is on a mission to help his friends find the perfect Christmas present. Join Rudy on his quest and see if you’re on Santa’s naughty or nice list! Tinsel the Tree is finally free to bust a move! Hop aboard a train ride through the beautiful redwood forest and join him as he tries out his new dance moves. Join the studio audience of this lively late-night talk show to hear the latest and greatest from Diva the Elf as she welcomes a very special rising star. Experience the magic of the holidays like never before! Meet our new friends Rudy the Polar Bear, Mrs. Claus, Tinsel the Tree, Skitter the Mouse and a band of Santa’s reindeer as they share their wishes with Santa Claus himself. This lively, family-friendly show is included with park admission and runs several times each night. Come sing and dance along to help everyone find their wish for Santa—and watch as Santa makes their dreams come true with a sprinkle of Christmas magic! Experience the magic with jolly characters, lively shows, ice skating under the stars, festive food and drinks, dazzling light displays, and so much more!

sourceDescriptionRaw: Please join us for a Pow Wow dance demonstration by Ohiya celebrating Native American Heritage Month! You will learn about the songs, dances, art, food, and traditions of the Indigenous Peoples of America. Ohiya is a cultural collaboration of Native American Singers, Dancers and Artists from the greater San Francisco Bay Area. Guided by our mission: honoring our ancestors and their teachings through cultural expressions of the past, present and future, our group strives to educate people of the songs, dances, art, food, and ways of life of the Indigenous Peoples of America. The group was founded to promote and celebrate the beauty and tradition of Native American social dance and singing styles commonly viewed at Pow Wows.This program is for all ages, and no registration is required!nbsp;\nFor accessibility accommodations (ex. Looking for cute, fun, creative, and crafty wares? Check out the ARTrepreneur: Teen Craft Fair. All teens featured at this Fair have complete the ARTrepreneur entrepreneur program and are small business owners. Come support them and check out their incredible products.
Cash and most payment apps accepted.nbsp;No obligation to purchase.
The Fair will be held during the TeenHQ Theater Production.
Scheduled Vendors
Fuzzy and Fluffy
Fuzzy and Fluffy will be selling popular crocheted items, including loaf cats, octopi, and chickens. Keychain items like the mini octopus, mushroom pops, and mini chickens. These items are perfect as birthday or holiday gifts, or even room decor! We're looking forward to meeting you at our market!
Green Apple Boutique
Welcome to Green Apple Boutique! We are a small business located in the Bay Area and would love to have you as a part of our community! Our shop is currently focusing on the production of pins and jewelry but we plan to expand our inventory to cute stationary in the future!
Lils Creations
Lils Creations features handmade jewelry, customized stationery, beadable pens, unique keychains and charms. Designed with care, high-quality materials, and a touch of character-inspired charm, my items are crafted to offer thoughtful, one-of-a-kind gifts and accessories.
Calderon Co
Calderon Co Logo
This endeavor is the amalgamation of a love for toys, 3D printing, and making money. The goal was to create a toy that could satisfy the urge to fidget or imagine new, forbearing the spontaneous horrors of a bored mind, without being a traditional, hyper-consumeristic toy that serves little purpose beyond draining your wallet. Three main problems were identified, alongside a single solution: affordable toys suck, they don't keep people still, and the CEO of CC is very broke. The solution? A selection of 3D-printed fidget toys, tested profusely. What makes this selection unique is that people of all ages can come to the table and try the fidgets firsthand. Every effort is made to ensure product quality through careful selection of what gets sold, and by personally breaking them in so the initial rough texture is ameliorated as much as possible.
AydrawArt
AyDraw Logo
AydrawArt crafts creations take the ease- and add some style. We create practical trinkets such as beautiful handmade keychains, pipe cleaner flowers, cards, cups, jewelry bowls, and so much more all to inspire your creative flame! For reasonable prices add some bling and express your individuality and creativity today!Two Tiny PotatoesSelling yarn-crafted items including star wands, keychains, flower hair clips, arm cuffs, coasters, and hand warmers.Forever FlowersForever Flowers LogoForever Flowers blends the beauty of bouquets with everlasting love from crocheting, which makes it the perfect gift for yourself or others to commemorate a moment with. Forever Flowers offers a wide range of crocheted products from flowers, coasters, plants and more that can be used for many different purposes.
nbsp;
nbsp;
Learn about the ARTrepreneur program and how teens bring their small business dreams to life.

title: Everyone Can Create: Let's Create a Beat! Using GarageBand
description: Have you ever been interested in making your own song?
parentSummary: Have you ever been interested in making your own song?
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Have you ever been interested in making your own song? Join us in learning how to make beats and become songwriters! In this program for beginners, we will be using GarageBand to create our own songs with drum pads and Apple Loops. Open to everyone in grades 3-6. 
Everything needed for this course will be provided, but you are more than welcome to bring your own personal iPad with the free GarageBand app downloaded, especially if you want to save your work.
Free. Registration is recommended.
This series is taught in English only.
Registration closes at 12pm the day before class. However, if seats are still available, students in grades 3-6 can walk in on Saturday if they arrive before 3pm to sign in. Maximum class size is 25.
Although the class is scheduled from 3-4:30pm, students who finish their projects early are welcome to leave early.
ADA Accommodation Requests
Sábado, 21 de noviembre de 2026 | 3:00–4:30 p. m.
¿Alguna vez has querido crear tu propia canción? ¡Acompáñanos a aprender cómo crear ritmos y convertirte en compositor! En este programa para principiantes, utilizaremos GarageBand para crear nuestras propias canciones con pads de batería y Apple Loops. Dirigido a estudiantes de 3.º a 6.º grado.
Todo lo necesario para este curso será proporcionado, pero puedes traer tu propio iPad personal con la aplicación gratuita GarageBand descargada, especialmente si deseas guardar tu trabajo.
Gratis. Se recomienda registrarse con anticipación.
Esta serie será enseñado únicamente en Inglés.
La inscripción cierra a las 12 p.m. el día antes de la clase. Si quedan espacios disponibles, los alumnos de grado 3 a 6 pueden venir el sábado e inscribirse antes de las 15:00 p.m. La clase tiene un cupo máximo de 25 alumnos.
Aunque la clase está programada de 3-4:30 p.m., los alumnos que terminan sus proyectos antes podrán retirarse si lo desean.
Solicitudes de adaptaciones ADA
Tất cả chúng ta đều có thể sáng tạo: Hãy tạo nên nhịp điệu! Sử dụng GarageBand
Thứ Bảy, ngày 21 tháng 11 năm 2026, từ 3 - 4:30 giờ chiều
Quý vị đã bao giờ muốn tự sáng tác bài hát chưa? Hãy tham gia cùng chúng tôi để học cách tạo beat và trở thành nhạc sĩ! Trong chương trình dành cho người mới bắt đầu này, chúng ta sẽ sử dụng GarageBand để tạo ra những bài hát của riêng mình với những trống và Apple Loops. Lớp học dành cho học sinh lớp 3-6.
Mọi thứ cần thiết cho khóa học này sẽ được cung cấp, nhưng bạn hoàn toàn có thể mang theo iPad cá nhân của mình với ứng dụng GarageBand miễn phí đã tải xuống, đặc biệt khi bạn muốn lưu tác phẩm của mình.
Miễn phí. Xin vui lòng ghi danh trước.
Lớp học được chỉ dạy hoàn toàn bằng tiếng anh.
Thời hạn ghi danh kết thúc vào 12 giờ trưa ngày trước khi lớp học bắt đầu. Tuy nhiên, nếu vẫn còn chỗ trống, học sinh lớp 3-6 có thể đến trực tiếp vào thứ Bảy nếu đến trước 3 giờ chiều để điểm danh. Lớp học tối đa là 25 học sinh.
Mặc dù lớp học được lên lịch từ 3 đến 4 giờ 30 chiều, nhưng học sinh nào hoàn thành bài tập sớm có thể về sớm.

With Kathak dance as their medium, Noorani Dance is committed to enlightening minds and hearts through the arts.

title: San José Youth Commission Meeting
description: Want to learn about local government and issues affecting youth in San Jose?
parentSummary: Want to learn about local government and issues affecting youth in San Jose?
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Want to learn about local government and issues affecting youth in San Jose? Join us at the San Jose Youth Commission meeting!
This in-person eventnbsp;will consist of discussions about city policies, city department reports,nbsp;Youth Commissioner district reports, and more.nbsp;The minutes and agendas are linked here.
The Youth Commission meets on the 4th Monday of the month, beginning at 6:30 PM. The Youth Commission does not meet in the months of July or December.nbsp;
Meetings are predominantly held in person at Council Chambers in City Hall and are also streamednbsp;virtually, but always refer to the meeting agenda to confirm the meeting location.
Thenbsp;San Jose Youth Commissionnbsp;is recognized as the official youth advisory group to the Mayor and City Council. Youth Commissioners develop policy recommendations concerning youth and support youth who serve their community through civic engagement and participation.ADA Accommodation Requests

description: Join us for music, stories, and joyful playnbsp;at this storytime perfect for families with young children.
parentSummary: Join us for music, stories, and joyful playnbsp;at this storytime perfect for families with young children.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Join us for music, stories, and joyful playnbsp;at this storytime perfect for families with young children. Music and movement help our littlest learners develop their communication skills, their imagination, and their connection with the loving grown-ups in their lives. Let's sing!Free, with limited capacity.
Vehicle parking may be limited. A small number of strollers may be parked outside the Children's Room; no strollers in storytime, please.
Sensory Notes:
- Sound: This storytime will be noisy with singing, instruments, and pre-recorded music. Let the librarian know before storytime begins if you would like to borrow a pair of ear defenders for your child.
- Visuals: This storytime is usually very busy with lots of families moving around.
- Texture: This storytime sometimes includes the use of soft scarves, weighted beanbags, and other textured items. Children are always free to skip these activities if they prefer.
Need a social story? Email charlie.roos@lib.sccgov.org to request a digital social story to help your child feel prepared for storytime.
For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

sourceDescriptionRaw:
This student-led program, Paws and Play, brings young students together to create handmade toys and blankets for the dogs and cats at our San Martin Animal Services Center. The aim of this programnbsp;is to provide comfort, joy, and entertainment to animals still waiting for their forever home, and to give participants an opportunity to make a positive impact on their community!
Basic sewing skills are highly encouraged, but not necessary. We highly recommend that the parents of younger children stay to assist their child with their project. All supplies will be provided.
This program is for kids ages 8-12. Registration is required do to space limitations. Walk ins will be accepted if space is available.This program is an approved Passion Project Proposal and will be led by Andria Perez,nbsp;a Morgan Hill high school student volunteering to share their passions with the community!
For any questions, please contact Librarian Hannah Clement at hannah.clement@lib.sccgov.org
For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

title: After-School STEaM at Almaden
description: Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego® bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges.
parentSummary: Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego® bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Drop in on Tuesday afternoons in at 4:30 p.m. for a new STEaM adventure every week. Active engagement with STEaM promotes academic success.nbsp;
Topic list is subject to change, please check back or call the branch for up-to-date details. Suggested ages vary, please refer to individual program descriptions.
Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program.
Aug 18 -nbsp;The Science of Soap: Floating Drawing Pepper ExperimentParticipants will learn about the properties of soap, how it cleans and why that's important by creating their own floating drawings and playing with adhesion and repulsion properties of pepper and soap.
Aug 25 -nbsp;nbsp;Logic GamesWork individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles.***please note that the Mental Math: Multiplication program has been RESCHEDULED for Sept 22 and the other math topics have moved accordingly***
Sept 1 -nbsp;Marble Run FunHarness the force of gravity as you create your own marble run.
Sept 8 - Lego Engineering Challenge (***please note topic change***)In this workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego® bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up.
 Volcanoes (will be rescheduled at a later time)Learn about the different types of volcanoes and create your own eruption with common household ingredients.
Sept 15 - Spike Robotics Code Quest Learn to code a pre-built Lego Spike robot to move around and collect components using a block-based coding language similar to Scratch.
Sept 22 -nbsp;Mental Math:nbsp;MultiplicationChildren have the opportunity to learn and practice multiplication skills with a focus on understanding how multiplication works and is related to addition.
Oct 6 - Wind Turbine EngineeringIn this hands-on workshop, participants will build their own working wind turbines using everyday household items. Through fun, interactive experiments, they will test different designs and observe the impact of tweakable variables on performance. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation.
Oct 13 - Paper RocketsLearn what makes rockets fly high and far! Then join us in making a rocket of your own that can fly the furthest!nbsp;Participants will learn about propulsion and list then create their own rockets.
Oct 20 -nbsp;Properties of Water (Science from Scientists)Participants will explore cohesion, adhesion andnbsp;surface tension through a series of simple activities that encourage them to investigate and make observations about the unique propertiesnbsp;of water.
Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Children younger than age 9 must be accompanied by an adult caregiver during this program.
Oct 27 - TBA
Nov 3 -nbsp;Learn About Aerodynamics Through Paper PlanesIn this high-flying workshop, participants will build different types of paper planes and learn concepts of aerodynamics and impact of plane design through fun and interactive experiments. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation.
Nov 10 - Ozobot Maze RunnerTeach your Ozobot to navigate a maze using simple color codes.
Nov 17 -nbsp;Logic GamesWork individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles.
Nov 24nbsp;-nbsp;TBA
Dec 1 -nbsp;Let's Build ParachutesIn this workshop, participants will build parachutes of different shapes, sizes and material, and observe the impact of their design. They will participate in fun parachute drops with different loads while learning the science behind parachute design. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation.
Dec 8 -nbsp;Lego Engineering ChallengeIn thisnbsp;workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego® bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up.

sourceDescriptionRaw: Mindfulness meditation is a wonderful way to develop clarity, discipline, and perspective as well as improve your mental and physical health. Join online sessions with Phuong Pham, a Buddhist nun experienced in the practice of meditation. Each session is 45 minutes of meditating together followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and QA led by Phuong. The group sharing and QA is a valuable part of the process, so participants can reflect on the meditation session together and build community. title: TeenHQ MakerSpace Studio
registrationEvidence: Pre-registration is recommended to reserve your spot.
description: Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, GlowForge, Sewing Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies.
parentSummary: Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, GlowForge, Sewing Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Middle and high schoolers: Come explore the TeenHQ MakerSpace! Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, GlowForge, Sewing Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies. Work with our teen librarian to bring your idea to life. Each machine and other materials have limitations and time requirements. Please see below for more information. Pre-registration is recommended to reserve your spot. If not all claimed registration spots have arrived by 4:30PM, they will be given to those waiting. All services are provided for free to middle and high school (6-12 grade) students. Younger people and adults are not permitted in the area unless required to assist with a disability. 
Pre-registration will start 1 week before the start of the program. Please un-register yourself if you find you're unable to attend at a later date.nbsp;Registration closes 1 hour before the start of the program. There will not be a waitlist for pre-registration. Drop-ins will be accepted if not all registration slots are filled and if not all registered individuals arrive by 4:30PM.nbsp;The area is wheelchair accessible from the Children’s Room elevator. Other accommodations can be made available with request.nbsp;ADA Accommodation RequestsPlease note that each device requires time to set up, use, and complete whatever task you're wanting to use the space for. Be sure that you have enough time in your schedule to attend the program. Not all tasks may be completed before the end of the program and you may need to return to get your completed items or pause your task and restart at another studio session. We appreciate your patience and flexibility.
3D Printing: All requested prints must take less than 4.5 hours to print. All requested prints will need to be picked up at a later date. Contact information is required for notification of pick-up. 3D print quality and time needed to complete prints is not guaranteed. Multiple objects can be printed as long as the total time does not exceed 4.5 hours. 
Poster Printing: All prints must be assembled on a 2”x3” canvas and printed as a.png. Please see the regularly scheduled poster printing event for further details. One poster per teen per day. 
GlowForge: Create a custom engraved object. Object should follow similar guidelines to the Custom Keychain Program. Complexity of request is at the discretion of the librarian. 
Sewing Serger Machines: It is recommended that you bring your own fabric and thread if fabric is special or color is a factor. There are scrap material and thread available but we cannot guarantee material quality or availability. An iron and ironing board is also available 
Cricut: Basic Cricut supplies are available, such as construction and cardstock paper. If your project is specialized, such as requiring iron-on, you’ll need to bring your own materials. It is recommended that you know the requirements for any materials you provide. 
Button Press: TeenHQ offers two sizes of button presses. We cannot offer printing. If your bring your own printout of buttons, it must be printed on standard printer paper. Paper thicker than standard printer paper cannot be used on the button presses. All measurements below are diameter length in inches. 
Small Button Press: 1.25” Large Button Press: 2.25” Picture Size: 1.156” Cut Line: 1.629” Picture Size: 2.063” Cut Line: 2.625”

parentSummary: Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season.
sourceDescriptionRaw: | Performances: December 2-3, 2026 | A holiday mash-up for the whole family, The Hip Hop Nutcracker returns for another spectacular tour. Directed and choreographed by Tony and Olivier Award-nominated Jennifer Weber, this contemporary dance spectacle is a re-mixed and re-imagined version of the classic, smashing hip hop dance and Tchaikovsky’s timeless music together into a heart-stirring and inspirational holiday event. The Hip Hop Nutcracker is brought to life by a powerhouse cast of a dozen all-star dancers, a DJ, a violinist, and MC Kurtis Blow, one of hip hop’s founding fathers, who opens the show with a short set. Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season. Innovative digital graffiti and visuals transform the landscape of E.T.A. Hoffmann’s beloved story from traditional 19th Century Germany to the vibrant, diverse sights and sounds of contemporary New York City. Grab your family and friends and let the dynamic performers of The Hip Hop Nutcracker take you on a journey that celebrates love, community and the magic of the holiday season. Performances: ● Wed., December 2, 2026 @ 7:00pm ● Thur., December 3, 2026 @ 7:00pm > CPA Events Calendar > Visitor FAQs

sourceDescriptionRaw: Vamos a celebrar la época dorada del cine mexicano entre 1930 y 1960 con un ciclo de cine dedicado al cine de oro mexicano. Inolvidables películas protagonizadas por estrellas como Pedro Armendáriz, María Félix, Dolores del Río, Pedro Infante, Cantinflas entre otras y otros. Venga con su familia y amigos para disfrutar por primera vez o de nuevo con las películas que emocionaron a varias generaciones con sus poderosas historias y una fotografía en un expresivo blanco y negro. Para inaugurar el ciclo, el domingo 6 de diciembre, vamos a mostrar Gugambilia; protagonizada por Dolores del Río y Pedro Armendáriz a las dos de la tarde. Después de la película habrá una breve discusión sobre su historia, realización y temática. ¡Habrá meriendas para disfrutar de la película! We will celebrate the golden age of classic Mexican cinema between 1930 and 1960, with a series dedicated to several movies from this period. Unforgettable movies starred by luminaries such Pedro Armendáriz, María Félix, Dolores del Río, Pedro Infante, Cantinflas among others. Come with your family and friends to enjoy the movies that move various generations with their powerful storytelling and their beautiful black and white cinematography full of expression. To begin the series, we will show Gugambilia starring Dolores del Río and Pedro Armendáriz from 2 to 4:30 pm on December 6. After the movie, there will be a brief discussion about the movie’s history, its making and themes. There will be snacks to enjoy with the movie! For accessibility accommodations (ex. sourceDescriptionRaw: Do you have what it takes to be a Tech Detective? Juniors and Cadettes will begin by practicing the art of forensic drawing by sketching a “suspect” as described by a “key witness.” Next, they learn about & practice codes and fingerprinting.
